video_title: Have Nuggets, Celtics, Wolves, 76ers Expired? LeBron's Future + More  | ALL NBA PODCAST

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons' season was a success despite identified holes

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: I think it still goes down as a success because they won a playoff series, which is something they hadn't done since 2008. But look, this was the number one seed. They went down 3-1 to Orlando. They went down 3-2 in this series. Now they forced a Game 7 with an amazing win on the road. But they clearly had nothing left, and Donovan Mitchell has put on a show. And this Cavs team that have really been, they've been under the microscope and have been just crushed all season and postseason long. This is quite a statement Game 7 from the Cavs. At least the Pistons can say, we're young. We didn't make a move at the trade deadline beyond bringing in Kevin Huerter. They really took the Oklahoma City approach from two years ago. They wanted to give this group a playoff run, and some clear holes were identified and exposed. I mean, they need more shooting. Duren did not play anywhere near his regular season level. The guy's probably going to end up on an All-NBA team because of all the injuries in this league this year. We very rarely saw All-NBA play from him in these playoffs. So the Pistons certainly have questions, but the questions that the Cavs avoid by winning this game so handily, or at least putting on the shelf for one more round, I mean, the Cavs, had the Cavs lost this Game 7 after taking a 3-2 lead and being able to close this thing out at home, it would have been really uncomfortable for them immediately, like seconds after the buzzer. The Pistons can take a little bit more of a pragmatic approach, even though it is a disappointment. I mean, this, you know, this was a, there was a spot in the Eastern Conference Finals up for grabs for both of these teams, really, up for grabs. This was a coin flip series.

quotes.speaker: Adam Mares
quotes.summary_phrase: New CBA makes teams rise and fall faster
quotes.quote: I don't know about you. I'm spending a lot of time trying to figure out just the direction of the league and what these new CBAs and lottery reform and all that means about long-term contention. And it just feels to me, maybe it's because of my perspective in Denver, but it feels to me like teams are rising and falling faster than ever. Like you could pop up out of nowhere quick, and you could fall and crash to the ground faster than ever. And this Pistons run reminds me in many ways of the Nuggets' first run back in 2019. If you remember that one, Mark, they beat a not very good Spurs team in Round 1, but it took seven games. And they went to a not very good, but okay, Portland team, and it went seven games, and they lost Game 7 on their home court. So very much mirrors what the Pistons have done. But why I bring it up is, when I talk about rising and falling, I know everybody tries to look at this like arc. You have a great player in Cade, let's extend this for 10 years. But I almost wonder if it's, they might look back on this and say, what are the chances? How many Conference Finals is Cade Cunningham going to make in the next five seasons? Cade Cunningham and the Pistons, I should say. And I would set the line at one, you know, like it's so hard to do. And so if you had a chance now where you made it to a Game 7, I just think we'll look back at this three years from now and say, that was not a first year, take your time, he's into it. It was, if you're open, go for it, because you never know when you're going to fall out of contention in this new CBA.

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons have more flexibility than Nuggets under new CBA
quotes.quote: I'm with you and look, I think if you go back and look at our shows from February, I'm pretty sure I said I wish the Pistons would have been more aggressive because this East is so wide open. And in a way, it's been even more wide open than we anticipated because the way the Celtics finished the regular season, we thought, wow, okay, the Celtics have, they got Jayson Tatum back. They've now filled the void in a conference where we're, you know, we're struggling to pinpoint teams that we think can get to the Finals and give either the Thunder or a Spurs a good series. But the Pistons are still in the East, and unlike, you know, that's something that your Nuggets cannot say. And they do still have a lot of flexibility to make moves. They, like, they have not, they still have wiggle room, they still have financial flexibility, they still have draft chips to move around. So, like, whereas, you know, if you, if you want to compare this to Denver, which is obviously the team I think you, you know the best and that you're closest to, you know, the Nuggets have just been going all in, all in, all in to just try to get as good a team around Nikola Jokic as they could. They won one, but now the Nuggets are definitely on that list of teams that, like, they know their supporting cast isn't good enough, but they're lacking the flexibility to really change it. Detroit does have that.

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Duren's playoff struggles complicate his contract extension

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: I think the two votes are well deserved, by the way, in my opinion. I think Cade Cunningham is, I mean, he's appreciated quite a bit, but I, I just walk away from this thinking that that is one of the few guys I feel like you can build an entire roster around. He's that good. And for, and for Pistons fans, I do think they have a lot of excitement going forward. I don't think that they've, you know, hurt themselves or anything like that. It's just, I do think every team is going to look back after a three or four-year run with a core and say, man, that ended quicker than we thought because this new CBA just seems to have everybody on the run. Speaking of the new CBA, though, I am so curious what you are hearing about how you evaluate Duren after this playoffs because what a great year he had, improvement all around, but I don't think you can overstate how bad he was in this playoffs, or I should just say how ineffective he was in these playoffs. So what are people saying?

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Stein
text_blocks.text: Especially because at the end of the regular season, people are saying, you got to max this guy. You got to give him a huge max. And again, we saw very little of that All-NBA level in this series. So yes, that's one of the difficult decisions that Detroit is going to face. What are those negotiations with Duren going to look like? And so even though obviously you wouldn't say that Detroit wanted things to turn out this way, because obviously they wanted to go, they wanted to win this series and go to the Conference Finals. But you do wonder if for the long term, the money saved, the money that they presumably would be able to save now, I wonder if that does end up helping them in the long term, because if you max Duren, now you've, you know, that obviously, that obviously changes your flexibility equation.

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' financial limitations make their future murky
quotes.quote: First trip to the Conference Finals without LeBron James since 1992, long before the days that podcasts were possible. So yeah, I mean, the Game 5 performance, especially this performance, Donovan Mitchell having never been to a Conference Finals, this is a huge moment for him. I still think the Cavs, honestly, are going to face, like, the questions that they, unless, I mean, the Knicks to me have established themselves as deserved favorites in the East now. I think the Knicks win the next round. You know, will the Cavs be able to play freer in that series because they were so close to elimination in this one? Possibly. But just, just remember, Donovan Mitchell has a similar contract to Giannis Antetokounmpo, and he's contract extension eligible in July. If the Cavs don't get him signed to an extension, does that mean they start listening to trade offers for him? Their finances, they, they have, they, you know, they're the only second apron team in the league. So they're going to have to do something to loosen that up. And when they made the trade for James Harden at the trade deadline, it was instantly presumed around the league that he's getting a multi-year deal. Now that multi-year deal should come in at a lower annual number than the $39 million that Harden made this season. But the Cavs don't have financial flexibility. They don't have a lot of picks to make changes. Teams have been trying to get Jarrett Allen off them for a long time. Will they finally cave there? So, this was a huge step. I don't want to diminish it because Donovan Mitchell has had to hear over and over and over again about how he's never been to the Conference Finals, and he was great tonight. 15 points in that third quarter, even though he was racking up five fouls along the way. I mean, this is a monster win for the Cavs to do this on the road. But I would just say they, you know, again, Detroit is a younger team, younger in its evolution with a lot more flexibility. The Cavs have to get something done this spring. They have, like, they, like, if the Knicks beat them 4-1 or a sweep, Cleveland is right back in the position where we are criticizing them heavily.

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavs' spending won't influence other teams due to new CBA

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: Really? See, I, that's one of the questions I wanted to ask you was, does this just constitute a success because this is a big win? They knocked off the one seed. You're in the Conference Finals. But you still, I mean, and the Knicks are playing unbelievable basketball, man. In this playoffs, they have really reached their peak. And you're saying if they fall to that, it, it's throw it all out the window. You're still the most expensive roster.

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Stein
text_blocks.text: If it's, if it's a lopsided series. Now, if it's, you know, if that, if they take the Knicks six, seven, or if the Cavs go to the Finals, you know, I'll be the, I'll be the first one to hat tip them because I, I will, I am not, I think the Knicks are going to win that series. And, you know, I just, Cleveland's future is murky because of the finances. It's just, they are so expensive. And it's, you know, it's tough. Look, you're living this in Denver. Like, when you are expensive and you want to change things around, it's really hard to do that. It's really hard to do that. So, again, I do not want to rain on the Cavs' parade. This is a tremendous moment for them because I thought Detroit had reclaimed momentum in the series. Great win for the Cavs. Huge individual moment for Donovan Mitchell. But, you know, I, I see in chat, too, you know, Donovan Mitchell's going to be wanting a monster deal if you extend him, and he's, he's almost 30 now. So, there's a lot of question marks still in Cleveland, as great a night as this is for them. Well, another thing I wanted to ask you was, they are the most expensive roster. They're a second apron team, and I feel like all these owners are looking around, and general managers, too, are looking around and trying to understand, how bad is it if we go in the second round? Is it ever worth it? And I just wonder if you think it'll influence other teams to maybe look around and say, you know what, it worked for them, maybe it works for us. Let's spend and go in the second apron, even though we know all the penalties, you lose.

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: No. Honestly, I, look at Indiana. Now, the Pacers have caught so much hell for what they did with their first round pick and trading it for Ivica Zubac. And that pick falls out of the top four. And now you look at it, and you're like, oh my God, Indiana gave up number five in this draft, a 2029 unprotected first, and Benedict Mathurin, all of that for Ivica Zubac. Oh my God, this is so terrible. Why did they do this? And look, you can certainly make that case, and it's a defensible case. And the Clippers are going to get somebody really good at number five, and it might be painful. But the reason Indiana, there is nuance here. And the reason Indiana ultimately did it was because Ivica Zubac is a borderline All-Star, might be an All-Star center in the East, but he's only making $21 million. And that kind of contract is so valuable for a player that productive at that number. And Indy's calculus was, we got to give all this up now because if we wait till summer, there might be a bidding war for Ivica Zubac, and we might lose it. So I just cite that example just to show you, that's the way teams think. I'm going to overpay, and it is an overpay. But I'm going to overpay for a guy who can really produce on a team-friendly deal because if Ivica Zubac is an All-Star in the East at $21 million, and you got guys making 50 and 60, I mean, that's, that's why. That's the, that's what teams want to find. Those kind of players who you can call at $21 million, you can call a bargain.

quotes.speaker: Adam Mares
quotes.summary_phrase: Western Conference landscape is bleaker for teams like Nuggets and Timberwolves

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: The second apron is really a hard cap. It's not really a hard cap, but it really allows the owners to, to treat it as this hard cap. We can't do that. It's too risky. And it's just unfortunate, man. Um, let's talk about the teams that have expired here. So I think if we step back and look, the Nuggets, the Timberwolves, the Celtics, and the 76ers. If you're those four teams, you all considered yourself, with the, the 76ers, I think were tough because the health factor was such a variable for them, but the others, I think have been in this plateau where they've been up here, near the top or even at the top in some cases, and they've been hovering around. But I wonder if they all four of those teams, in your opinion, and just from what you're hearing around, do all four of those teams kind of feel like the ride is over? Not that they'll be bad if they run it back and stick to the formula, but that it's now looking more and more clear like their ceiling is not quite at the same level as the top teams in the NBA now.

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Stein
text_blocks.text: I have to point you again to the NBA map. When you are in the West, that landscape looks a lot more bleak. And that's why the Nuggets and the Wolves, who I think most people would say have been the best recent rivalry we've seen in this league, that came from nowhere. These two teams from the same division that met in the playoffs multiple times. Playoff series have been great between these teams. They, there's a real rivalry and animosity there. But again, get, making, you know, the, the Wolves have Anthony Edwards, and the Nuggets have Nikola Jokic. But the moves you need to make to refresh their supporting casts are so much harder because of the financial situations those teams are in. And again, because the Spurs and the Thunder, the Thunder and the Spurs, got to put the defending champs, got to put that in the right order till, you know, the Thunder are the defending champs. Like, they have set such a high bar, and you are, there's so much ground to make up to compete with those teams. And, and whereas the Celtics, as, as, you know, as inventive and bold as Brad Stevens has been, I just think somehow they're going to find a way to recharge themselves with a trade. And again, they're in the East. One move can move you up the ladder a lot quicker in the East than in the West. That is just reality.

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul George is more tradable than Joel Embiid

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: What do you anticipate the conversation being with Joel Embiid this offseason? Because I think it's actually interesting with him.

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Stein
text_blocks.text: I, I don't, I realistically there is no conversation. I just don't think. There's no market because of his injury. I mean, the contract, I mean, 50 plus million. Oh, 60. I mean, like, it's, it's just, I don't even think you can really, I, I, I can't imagine what sort of trade you could really assemble there. So, the good news for them is they have Tyrese Maxey. Edgecombe. Bob Myers just did a press conference and, and sure made it sound like he's going to be a lot more involved than we were anticipating with whoever comes in as Daryl Morey's replacement. And so I'm sure they'll be aggressive to try to make changes. Paul George, honestly, is much more tradable, I think, than Joel Embiid. He's in the, he's in the same contract situation as Trae Young was this past season. But the difference again is, Trae Young is much younger. Paul George is 36. But Paul George only has one year left on his deal guaranteed, then a player option. So let's, you know, I, I wouldn't promise it, but let's see, possibly, you know, possibly could a trade market emerge there? I, I would just say I think there's a better chance than a trade market emerging for Joel Embiid.

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James's future is uncertain due to financial limitations

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: Let's talk about LeBron James. Did you know, first of all, that I have two blazers from Quince? Did you know that? Do you? I did not know that. Did you really? And how do you like them?

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Stein
text_blocks.text: Fantastic. They don't, they didn't have my height for shirts. I'm like, I'm too tall. I'm 6'6", so I'm too tall for most, most places. They didn't have it.

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: Well, it's not really a flex. I'm telling you, I, I couldn't find the clothing. Um, let's talk about LeBron James. If you were to have told me two, like two months ago, before the playoffs started, the LeBron story, it just felt really open and shut. But he played so well in this playoffs, man. Like so well. And I, it, it, and it's not, you know, I'm not just saying this because it's exciting to talk about LeBron or this or that. He played in a way where I'm like, man, he could still be a very, I don't know if he could be the best player on a championship team, but he could certainly be the second best player on a championship team. So, um, is his future more interesting to you? And, and what's kind of the latest word on, on all the moving pieces around LeBron?

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Stein
text_blocks.text: It's been a huge topic. I was actually in LA Monday for the Lakers' elimination, and there was a lot of what I would say, just in case energy in the building. Just in case this is the last game. Like, you had to think it. I don't see, like, again, this is just my read. Only LeBron knows, and I'm not sure if LeBron himself knows yet, because it's not clear which team he's going to be playing for next season. But he was the best player in the Houston series. I just cannot see him walking away from the game. But the, the, the issue here is, and everyone's trying to figure this puzzle out, any team you want to list, whether it's going back to the Lakers, the dream storybook homecoming farewell tour in Cleveland, Knicks, Warriors, whatever scenario you want to come up with that you think LeBron James would find amenable, they have huge financial limitations. So, it's not easy for any of those teams to have LeBron on their roster next season. So that's why right now, in mid-May, it's really hard to forecast this. We might still be a good five, six weeks away from really knowing what his options are. I just, I don't know, man. I, I, I can't, I can't see this being it, even though he's 41, I just can't see it.

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron's playoff performance makes him still valuable

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: In part because, it's, it's funny, man. I was ready for LeBron to retire. I'll be honest. Just as a fan of the game, and in part because I thought maybe he had fallen too far. And I do think the 82-game season, it's not just him. A lot of guys, it's hard to get through the 82-game season. And I just wondered, like, maybe it is time to hang it up. But this playoff run, I watch him, and I go, man, he's still so good when it matters. When you, when he's able to play in this playoff rhythm, he's still so stinking good that I have to imagine a lot of teams would be after him. So if he is back, as I anticipate, is it going to be one of these things where we already know it's a handful, or is this as open as we've seen? LeBron's gone to free agency a handful of times now. Does this feel as open as it's, as it's been in really in recent history?

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Stein
text_blocks.text: No, because everyone knows he doesn't want to leave LA. Let's not forget, he's been a Laker for eight seasons. That's his longest continuous stretch with any one team in his career. So, nobody thinks he wants to leave. But the Lakers only have cap space if they let his $52 million get off the books, and then, you know, then they can try to go to work and, you know, they've been pointing to this upcoming summer for so long that this is the summer they're finally going to retool around Luka Doncic. So, can they do that and sign LeBron at a lesser number that he's okay with? Is LeBron, like, does LeBron really want to take a discount? That's something he's going to have to reckon with. Again, like, everyone talks about Cleveland. Why doesn't he just go back to Cleveland for a third marriage? He's been in LA so long. That, to me, that is a more, that is a more drastic move than it looks like on paper. Of course, he's played for the Cavs twice. He's from Northern Ohio, but he's been an Angeleno now for eight years, and I don't know that he's in a real rush to change that. So, like I said, it's, it's, when you, when I talk to people around the league and when I ask people who have studied LeBron or know LeBron much better than I do, pretty much everybody comes back with that same answer of, he's going to play one more year. But when you press and say where, nobody today can tell you where exactly.

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' long break could lead to rust, but also Anunoby's return

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: It'll be another summer of LeBron, as well as a summer of Giannis and, and, and, you know.

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Stein
text_blocks.text: Yeah, no, this, this whole summer, because free agency, as we know, all the action now happens really before free agency. But the, the trades, like, there is a huge chance that we're going to see significant trade activity because so many teams want to shuffle the pack and, and change their rosters around, and trades are going to be the only way they can do it.

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: Well, we'll see what happens there. Let me, uh, our last topic here, though, as we head to now the Conference Finals, there are some teams, and Oklahoma City is one of them. The Knicks are another that have just been sitting there waiting with their feet up. They might have taken a trip down to Cancun for a couple days. They could have gotten away with it. They have been able to rest. And I think personally that rest is actually huge in today's NBA in the playoffs. If you can get a series or two done early, it gives you a leg up. But because those two teams swept their series, you start to wonder, is rust actually a concern? They've been, they were, the Knicks in particular were in such a great rhythm that now they're taking, I don't know what it'll be, eight days off before they, between their last game and the next game. Is there a concern that rust will be better, bigger factor than rest will be?

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Stein
text_blocks.text: I actually like the rust for the Knicks because for one, they got to get OG Anunoby right, and the rest allows them to do that. And also, Cleveland's series with Detroit was such a roller coaster that I don't think Cleveland is, as great as tonight was, I don't know that Cleveland just bounces back with all kinds of life and spring in Game 1. Whereas Oklahoma City, it's interesting, there is this notion that Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is one of those guys who doesn't like an extended rest. And, and they had an extended rest after Round 1. And if you go back to Game 1 of the Lakers-Thunder series, the Lakers really applied a lot of pressure to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in Game 1 because they, they thought that that might be something that they could exploit, that, you know, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander doesn't love the idea of having such a long break. So, look, the Thunder are getting Jalen Williams back. Jalen Williams is off the injury report completely. They didn't have him at all in the second round. So that's got to be great news for the Thunder because you have to think they're going to need Jalen Williams to get past a Spurs team that beat them four times out of five during the regular season. But, yeah, I, I think, like, like I said, just, again, this is just one man's premonition. The Game 1 scores might prove me wrong, but I, I just think the Spurs have an opportunity to steal Game 1. Whereas I think the Knicks, also the Knicks, if Detroit wins the series, the Knicks start on the road. Now the Knicks are starting at home. They're probably getting OG Anunoby back. OG Anunoby's been practicing. The Knicks, this is their best chance to make the Finals in, they haven't been to the, the Knicks haven't been to the Finals since 1999. Just, I, I think MSG's going to be rocking, and I think the Cavs is going to be a, a whole different ball game for the Cavs in this next round.

quotes.speaker: Adam Mares
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's stock is up after playoff dominance
quotes.quote: I wanted to give my players who I think either have made a huge, had huge movement in their own personal stocks in this playoffs. I'm going to start with Victor Wembanyama. I've talked about him a lot, so I won't spend much time, but I just feel like his stock is way up. This is a big series for him against Oklahoma City. I had the question with him, he's dominant defensively. Offensively, he really figured himself out this year, in my opinion, really figured out how best to put pressure on defenses as an offensive player. But defensively, he was a juggernaut really since he walked into the league. And what I wondered about these playoffs was, could some team find something that is uncomfortable for him? Is there anything? And we're two rounds into this. Has it been the greatest offenses? The answer is no. He has the most comfortable he's ever been in these playoffs, absolutely dominant juggernaut. His stock to me is actually up, which I know is crazy to say for a guy who received MVP votes this year, but yet his stock is up.

quotes.speaker: Adam Mares
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren's stock is down after playoffs
quotes.quote: Jalen Duren, we've talked about him a lot. There's no question. He might have cost himself a lot of money with how he performed in these playoffs. Feel bad for him because I actually really like the guy.

quotes.speaker: Adam Mares
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamal Murray's stock is down after three straight playoff declines
quotes.quote: I think Jamal Murray, stock way down. Jamal Murray, and it's tough because this is his first All-Star season. I think he's going to be All-NBA, and yet, at the end of the year, his stock is down, not up, because how much he was erased in the playoffs, I think that he is now a player that you look at. I mean, playoff Jamal. This was a thing we all talk about. Three straight years, Jamal Murray has slid in the playoffs, not risen. So this idea of Jamal Murray, which was very true for the first half of his career, this playoff riser, kind of the ultimate playoff riser. Unfortunately, now we're talking about three years in a row where he has been a playoff faller. And I think now you have to wonder if that guy still is even capable of elevating to championship level the way he was for the Denver Nuggets.
